parsed.headline: Iranians express anxiety over potential return to all-out war amid US and Israeli election cycles

pages.text: According to reporting by Arab News, many residents in Iran are bracing for a possible return to all-out war as leaders in Israel and the United States increase threats ahead of upcoming elections in both nations. In Tehran, residents described growing anxiety to the Associated Press, with some preparing to leave the capital and others, such as 35-year-old Fereshteh Hajipour, stockpiling food and medicine due to fears of larger bombs and conflict. 1. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who faces a close vote on October 20, 2026, has stated that Iran’s leadership must be eliminated. 2. US President Donald Trump has vowed to “finish the job” in Iran eight months after the war began, as thousands of troops and a third aircraft carrier move toward the region. 3. Sasan Karimi, a former government official and foreign policy professor at the University of Tehran, stated that Iranian leadership believes President Trump will likely order new strikes regardless of the results of the US midterm elections. 4. Iran has threatened new targets, including undersea data cables in the Strait of Hormuz and US military bases and allies in the Middle East. This follows a month that has seen the highest number of reported attacks on commercial ships transiting the strait since the war began in March. Additionally, Iran’s president has accused the US of disrupting negotiations that have shown little progress for months.

parsed.headline: Nine killed and 40 injured after gunmen open fire at church funeral in Jordan

pages.text: Nine people were killed and 40 others were injured after gunmen opened fire during a funeral at St George’s Greek Orthodox church in Hamoud, located in the Karak governorate of Jordan, on October 23, 2026. Authorities described the attack on the country’s Christian minority as a terrorist act carried out by extremists. While Interior Minister Mazin Al Farrayeh stated the attack was performed by extremists, he noted it was too early to determine if they had links to known groups inside or outside Jordan. There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the shooting. The church is situated approximately 90 kilometers (55 miles) south of the capital, Amman. Jordan’s Prime Minister, Jafar Hassan, characterized the event as a result of terrorist ideology and blind extremism. Maj. Gen. Abdallah al-Maaytah, head of Jordan’s Public Security Directorate, stated that the hunt for the attackers was continuing and that most of those injured were receiving treatment.

Footage broadcast on Jordan’s state-owned Al-Mamlaka television station, which was verified by Reuters, showed three people firing at the church from a pavement and hiding behind trees and a low wall before running toward the entrance. While state TV footage depicted three attackers, a witness reported hearing that other people saw four gunmen; the Associated Press noted it could not independently verify the total number of assailants. One mourner, Dorgham Halasa, stated that intense gunfire erupted 15 minutes after the funeral began. A priest at the scene described ordering people to get to the ground as the shooting occurred. Witness video showed broken glass and pools of blood on the church floor. A government statement confirmed that investigations are underway, though it did not specify if any gunmen had been captured or killed.

parsed.headline: Bangladesh Home Minister says next national election will be held under caretaker government

pages.text: Bangladesh Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated on October 25, 2026, that the next national election will be held under a caretaker government. Speaking at a press briefing at the home ministry, Ahmed said a political consensus has been reached on the issue and that the system would be formally restored through a constitutional amendment. He noted that the Supreme Court had judicially revived the caretaker government system by overturning an earlier judgment by Justice Khairul Haque regarding the 13th amendment, though a formal amendment remains necessary for restoration. Ahmed described the restoration of the system as a commitment and a demand of their movement.

parsed.headline: Albertans approve immigration questions but reject constitutional reforms in referendum

pages.text: In a referendum in Alberta, Canada, voters approved five immigration-related questions but rejected constitutional reforms, according to results from the United Conservative government's nine-question ballot. Elections Alberta reported that the count, which involved hand-counting 20,574,612 ballots, was completed on the night of October 24, 2026. The agency noted this was approximately three days later than the intended deadline set under provincial referendum regulations. Elections Alberta stated this was the highest number of ballots ever hand-counted in a Canadian electoral event. Official results, including total voter turnout, are scheduled to be made official in October. 1. The question requiring proof of citizenship to vote in provincial elections received 58 per cent support. 2. Approximately 55 per cent of voters supported a pitch for the province to take greater control of immigration to decrease the number of newcomers. 3. Three questions regarding methods for limiting public and social services to certain non-permanent residents received 52, 52.6, and 53 per cent support, respectively. While results were still being processed on October 21, 2026, Alberta Premier Danielle Smith told reporters she would prioritize adjusting the province's approach to economic migrants but would proceed with caution on other immigration matters. Smith stated she wanted to be cautious because changing rules midstream can be difficult for those who arrived with certain expectations. Lori Williams, a political scientist at Mount Royal University, noted a rural-urban divide regarding the nine questions and expressed doubt that the results represented the strong mandate the government sought.

parsed.headline: Amnesty International accuses Israel of unlawful attacks and property destruction in Syria

pages.text: On October 23, 2026, Amnesty International accused Israel of carrying out deadly military attacks and the unlawful destruction of civilian property in Syria. Erika Guevara Rosas, Amnesty International’s senior director for research, policy, advocacy and campaigns, stated that decades of impunity for Israeli actions have encouraged violations extending to Lebanon and Syria. Guevara Rosas urged governments to use diplomatic and economic measures to pressure Israel to comply with international humanitarian law and hold the Israeli government accountable for its actions. These remarks were made ahead of Israel’s parliamentary elections, which are scheduled for October 27, 2026. The organization also called for an arms embargo, an end to the unlawful occupation of Palestinian territory, and the suspension of the EU-Israel Association Agreement.

parsed.headline: Amnesty International accuses Israel of unlawful attacks and property destruction in Syria

pages.text: On October 23, 2026, Amnesty International accused Israel of carrying out deadly military attacks and the unlawful destruction of civilian property in Syria. Erika Guevara Rosas, Amnesty International’s senior director for research, policy, advocacy and campaigns, stated that decades of impunity for Israeli actions have encouraged violations extending to Lebanon and Syria. Guevara Rosas urged governments to use diplomatic and economic measures to pressure Israel to comply with international humanitarian law and hold the Israeli government accountable for its actions in the region. These remarks were made ahead of Israel’s parliamentary elections, which are scheduled for October 27. Amnesty International also called for an arms embargo and the suspension of the EU-Israel Association Agreement as part of broader efforts to ensure accountability and end the unlawful occupation of Palestinian territory.

In a separate statement on October 23, 2026, Syria’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Ibrahim Olabi, condemned Israeli aggressions in Syria. Olabi reported that Israel continued violations and incursions in southern Syria and bombed sites inside the country on the same day that International Atomic Energy Agency Director General Rafael Grossi visited Syria to follow up on efforts regarding the nuclear file. Amnesty International's Guevara Rosas also noted that Israeli attacks in Lebanon have killed thousands of people, destroyed homes and civilian infrastructure, and resulted in the forced displacement of tens of thousands of civilians from southern Lebanon.

parsed.headline: President Mahama commissions new milk production line in Tema, Ghana

pages.text: President John Dramani Mahama commissioned a new evaporated milk production line at the Nestlé Ghana Limited factory in Tema on October 8, 2026. During the event, the president described Nestlé Ghana Limited as an institution integrated into the lives of multiple generations of Ghanaians, citing brands such as Ideal Milk, Milo, Cerelac, Nescafé, and Carnation as familiar household products. He used personal memories of consuming Ideal Milk in meals like tea, koko, and rice water to illustrate the relationship between the company's brands and Ghanaian families. While household spending in Ghana's fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) market increased by 12.9 per cent in 2025, research from Worldpanel by Numerator’s Brand Footprint suggests a gap remains in consumer reach. Findings indicate that 82 per cent of the country's top 250 FMCG brands reached fewer than half of Ghanaian households, despite the growth in spending.

parsed.headline: Three people injured in tiger attack near Bangladesh-India border

pages.text: Three residents of Amjhol village were injured in a tiger attack on Sunday evening near the Amjhol border in Hatibandha upazila, Lalmonirhat, Bangladesh, according to reports from UNB cited by The Financial Express. The animal reportedly crossed into Bangladesh from India near the border area, which falls under the jurisdiction of the Bonchouki Border Outpost in Gotamari Union. Local reports state that Sharifa Begum was attacked by the tiger while searching for a goat; Afsar Hossain and Nazrul Islam were also injured while attempting to rescue her. The three individuals were taken to a local hospital and subsequently transferred to Rangpur Medical College Hospital for advanced treatment. Lieutenant Colonel Mehedi Imam, commander of the Lalmonirhat 15 BGB Battalion, confirmed the injuries and stated that the Forest Department had been informed and security in the area had been strengthened.

parsed.headline: Israeli election contender Gadi Eisenkot vows unity as Benjamin Netanyahu campaigns on security credentials

pages.text: In Tel Aviv, Israeli election contender and former army chief Gadi Eisenkot held his final major rally on October 25, 2026, vowing to heal divisions within Israeli society. Eisenkot pledged a commitment to the economy and security, stating his goal is to bring together all Israelis, including those who did not vote for him. He also pledged to establish a state commission of inquiry into the failings that led to the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023, which occurred under the current administration. According to Arab News, Eisenkot has cast Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as unfit to lead. Prior to a ban on new polling that took effect on October 20, 2026, polls had shown Netanyahu and Eisenkot running neck and neck in the election race. Netanyahu has campaigned on his security credentials and sought to characterize Eisenkot as soft on Iran and beholden to Arab interests.
